_comment: Site-only text for wadamesh.com/apps.html. Names, versions and requirements come from deploy/apps/apps.json (the Store catalog); scripts/build/gen-apps-page.py merges the two at every site deploy. One entry per app id. No em dashes.

monitor.tagline: Your channel at a glance, and every packet you hear.
monitor.about: Live RSSI and noise as tiles and a filled chart, with the noise floor dashed underneath, and the packets heard most recently with their type, signal bars, SNR and hop count. Tap a packet for its details: who sent it, the route it took, how far its SNR sat above what your spreading factor can still decode, its size and how long it was on the air.
highlights: Margin above the decode limit, per packet
Works with keys and trackball too

airtime.tagline: How busy the channel really is.
airtime.about: The live channel load as a big figure, the average and peak over the session, and your own time on the air. A filled chart shows the load against your region's duty-cycle limit, and a bar splits the airtime into what you received and what you sent. While it runs it keeps a Home widget with the load up to date.
highlights: Home widget while it runs (not on the 2 MB Heltec V4)

wardrive.tagline: Survey your coverage while you drive or walk.
wardrive.about: Every 20 seconds it sends a discovery probe that every node in earshot answers, and logs each reply with your GPS position, altitude and both directions of the link: how well you heard them and how well they heard you. The run goes to a CSV you can take off the device, and it plots back on the map so you can check coverage before you drive it again.
highlights: CSV log with position and altitude

ping.tagline: Round-trip time to any contact, with distance and bearing.
ping.about: Sends a ping as a direct message and measures how long the answer takes. Both devices swap their GPS position, so the result shows the round-trip time, the distance and the bearing when both have a fix. It also answers pings from other people running Ping.
highlights: Distance and bearing when both have GPS

mecp.tagline: Emergency messages everyone can read in their own language.
mecp.about: Writes and reads messages in the Mesh Emergency Communication Protocol. Pick a severity and the codes (injury, flooding, need water and many more), add the number of people and your position, and post it to the channel you choose. MECP lines heard on your channels while the app is open are shown decoded in plain words.
highlights: Severity, codes, head count and position
Plain text, so it crosses any channel
mecp.credit_note: Code table: MECP by xiang-dev-1, CC BY 4.0

nearby.tagline: Your contacts on a real map, nearest first.
nearby.about: Shows the contacts that share a position on the firmware's own map tiles, sorted by distance, with the bearing to each one and a live count of the packets you hear. It is also the reference app for the SDK's map, list, geo and packet calls, so it is a good place to start reading code.
highlights: Real map tiles inside the app
Distance and bearing to each contact
Reference app for wada.map and wada.geo

gpscompass.tagline: A compass dial, the live GPS fix, and the way to a contact.
gpscompass.about: A heading dial with the live GPS fix underneath. On the ThinkNode M9 the heading comes from its magnetometer, with a calibration you run once by turning the device around; on other boards it uses your GPS course while you move. Pick a contact with a known position and it appears on the dial with its bearing and range.
highlights: GPS course on every other board
Bearing and range to a contact

tripodometer.tagline: A trip computer for your walk or ride.
tripodometer.about: Tracks the distance, time, speed and altitude of a trip from the GPS. Start and stop it as you go, reset it for the next trip, and it keeps your trip across app restarts.

protreck.tagline: An outdoor watch: sun, moon, stopwatch, timer and altitude.
protreck.about: Four tools you swipe between. Astro shows sunrise, sunset and the moon phase for where you are. Chrono is a stopwatch with laps, Timer a countdown with an alarm, and Alti your GPS altitude with its minimum, maximum and a trend graph.
highlights: Stopwatch with laps and a countdown timer

music.tagline: Your MP3s and WAVs from the SD card, with the screen off.
music.about: Plays the MP3 and WAV files in a Music folder on the SD card, three folder levels deep, so Music/Artist/Album works. Previous, play and pause, next, shuffle and repeat, and it keeps going through the list with the screen off. It follows the device's sound switch and volume, and message chimes stay quiet while a track plays.
highlights: Shuffle and repeat, one track or all
Keeps playing with the screen off
T-Deck, T-LoRa Pager, T-Display P4, Tanmatsu, T-Deck Max

snake.about: Eat the food, grow longer, do not bite yourself. Steer with swipes, the trackball or the arrow keys, and tap after a game over to play again. Small enough to read in one sitting, which makes it the SDK's first reference app.
highlights: Runs on every board, the Heltec V4 included
Reference app for wada.ui and wada.input

2048.tagline: The sliding-tile puzzle, with your best score kept.
2048.about: Slide the tiles, merge equal numbers and reach 2048. Swipe or use the trackball to move, tap to start again, and your best score is kept between games.

tetris.about: Swipe left and right to move, up to rotate and down to drop. On a keyboard the arrows move and rotate, and Enter or Space drops.

breakout.about: Move the paddle with swipes or the arrow keys, launch the ball with a swipe up or Enter, and clear every brick to reach the next level.

blackjack.tagline: Casino Blackjack, with your bankroll kept between sessions.
blackjack.about: Twenty-one against the dealer from a six-deck shoe. Hit, stand, double down and split, set your bet before each hand, and your bankroll is still there the next time you open the app. Play it by touch, on the keyboard (H, S, D, P) or with the trackball, and the table scales to the screen, the T-Display P4 included.

sdscan.tagline: Finds and removes Windows malware on the SD card.
sdscan.about: Written for the SD-card worm some ThinkNode M9 cards shipped with: a hidden autorun file and Windows programs disguised as shortcuts. They cannot run on a radio, but they run on the first Windows PC the card goes into. The firmware decides what counts as a threat, so the app can remove those files and nothing else: never map tiles, backups or chat history.
highlights: Firmware decides what is a threat

sdktest.tagline: For app makers: checks the extended SDK on your board.
sdktest.about: Runs through the extended Lua SDK on the board in your hand and shows the results on screen: capabilities, clock, battery, GPS, private files, audio, SD listing, crypto against published test vectors and channel discovery. A few buttons transmit test messages, so it is a bench tool rather than something to leave running.
highlights: Crypto checked against RFC test vectors
Every capability flag on one screen

spaceinvaders.tagline: The classic alien shooter, with your high score kept.
spaceinvaders.about: Shoot the descending rows before they land, hide behind the shields and hit the bonus UFO for extra points. Each cleared wave comes back faster. Move with swipes or the arrow keys and fire with a swipe up, a tap in the middle or the up key; your high score is kept between games.
